form.domainApexHelp: Enter the apex (example.com). SAN names are added as prefixes.
form.folderNameHelp: Unique identifier, can only contain letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens
form.emailFromAccount: Filled from the signed-in account email
form.certificatePlaceholder: Enter certificate content in PEM format or upload certificate file
form.privateKeyPlaceholder: Enter private key content in PEM format or upload private key file
form.sansHelp: Add a prefix and press Enter or +. The list shows full names such as www.example.com. Leave empty to apply for the apex only.
form.webrootHelp: Web root directory path for HTTP-01 verification, leave empty to use default path
form.forceRenewalHelp: If this apex already exists with the same SANs, you will be asked to overwrite. Different SANs always force a CA issue — disk cache is not used.
form.rateLimitInfo: Let's Encrypt limit: A maximum of 5 certificates can be issued for the same set of identifiers within 168 hours (7 days). If force renewal is enabled, the certificate will be re-applied even if not expired, which may trigger rate limits.
form.sectionImport: Import from file (parse only — PEM is not submitted)
form.sectionImportHint: Optional: upload an existing PEM to pre-fill domain, SANs, and issuer. That PEM is not sent to the server. Submitting runs Let's Encrypt issuance and stores the new cert on Edge.
form.sectionPemHint: Paste or upload PEM files. Edge stores this certificate as a manual import (POST /edge/tls/create).
form.dropPrivateKey: Drop a private key PEM here

upload.keyReadFailed: Could not read private key file
upload.parseFill: Parse PEM and fill domain / SANs

overwrite.message: Apex {{domain}} already has a certificate. Overwrite and replace it?

reapply.confirmMessageForce:
Are you sure you want to force re-apply certificate "{{domain}}"?
